questions.title: Greeting a New Programmer
questions.description:
Your very first Java program warm up. Read a name from input and print a two line greeting exactly as shown.

Input Format:
A single line containing one word: the name.

Output Format:
Hello, <name>!
Welcome to Java programming.

Constraints:
1 <= length of name <= 20

Welcome to Java programming.

Welcome to Java programming.
questions.output2:

questions.title: Literals and Computed Values
questions.description:
A quick drill on printing literals versus computed values. Read a word and an integer, then print four lines: the word as read, the count as read, the next count and double the count.

Input Format:
One line with a word and an integer separated by a space.

Output Format:
Word: <word>
Count: <count>
Next count: <count + 1>
Double count: <count * 2>

Constraints:
1 <= count <= 1000000

Count: 4
Next count: 5
Double count: 8

Word: Code
Count: 10
Next count: 11
Double count: 20

Double count: 2

Double count: 500

Next count: 1000000
Double count: 1999998

questions.title: Quoted Echo Printer

Line 1: the word wrapped in double quotes, for example "Java"

questions.title: Study Plan Tracker
questions.description:
An online platform tracks each learner journey through a 30 day Java plan. Read the student name on its own line, then the starting day and the number of days already completed, each on its own line. The plan always ends on day 30; report the end day and how many days remain.

Line 1: student name (may contain spaces)
Line 2: starting day (an integer)
Line 3: days completed (an integer)

Student: <name>

questions.title: App JVM Compatibility Checker
questions.description:
A deployment bot checks whether an app can run on the installed JVM before shipping. Read the app name, the JVM version the app requires and the installed JVM version. Print the check report; an upgrade is needed exactly when the installed version is lower than the required version.

Input Format:
One line with three tokens separated by spaces: app name (a single word), required JVM version (an integer), installed JVM version (an integer).

App: <app>

Installed JVM: <installed>
Upgrade needed: yes or no

questions.title: Sponsor Tier Report
questions.description:
An event finance tool sums sponsor contributions and assigns a partnership tier. Read the sponsor company name, the number of gold sponsors, the number of silver sponsors, the contribution per gold sponsor and the contribution per silver sponsor (all integers, in rupees). The base amount is goldCount * perGold + silverCount * perSilver. A bonus of one tenth of the base (integer division) is added. The tier is PLATINUM when the grand total is at least 100000, GOLD when it is at least 25000, otherwise SILVER.

Input Format:
One line with five tokens separated by spaces: company (a single word), goldCount, silverCount, perGold, perSilver (integers).

Output Format:
Sponsor: <company>
Base amount: <base>
Bonus amount: <base / 10>
Grand total: <base + bonus>
Tier: <PLATINUM or GOLD or SILVER>

Constraints:
0 <= goldCount, silverCount <= 1000, 1 <= perGold, perSilver <= 100000

questions.title: Character and Its ASCII Code

A char in Java is stored as a 16 bit unsigned number, so every character also has a numeric code. Read one character and print it along with its numeric ASCII code using an int cast.

A single line containing one character.

Output Format:
Char: <character>
ASCII: <numeric code>

Constraints:

questions.title: Integer vs Double Division
questions.description:
Integer division truncates the fraction, while converting an operand to double first keeps it. Read two integers a and b, then print a / b as plain integer division and (double) a / b formatted to exactly two decimal places.

Input Format:
One line with two integers a and b separated by a space.

Output Format:
Int division: <a / b>
Double division: <(double) a / b with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
-100000 <= a <= 100000, 1 <= b <= 1000

Double division: 3.50

Double division: 3.00

Int division: 0
Double division: 0.13

Int division: -3
Double division: -3.50

One line with two tokens: type name (one of byte, short, int, long, float, double, char, boolean) and item count (an integer).

Output Format:
Type: <type>
Items: <count>
Bytes: <count * size as a long>

Constraints:
type is one of the eight primitive names, 1 <= count <= 2000000000

questions.title: Cloud Storage Byte Converter
questions.description:
A cloud dashboard converts storage amounts into raw bytes for its billing system. Read a value and a unit (KB, MB or GB), then print the value, the unit and the size in bytes using the 1024 based ladder: 1 KB = 1024 bytes, 1 MB = 1024 KB, 1 GB = 1024 MB. Use long arithmetic so large values stay exact.

Input Format:
One line with two tokens: value (an integer) and unit (KB, MB or GB).

Output Format:
Value: <value>
Unit: <unit>
Bytes: <value converted to bytes as a long>

questions.title: Safe Addition Auditor
questions.description:
A banking batch job adds two large transaction values stored as long, and adding blindly can overflow the long range. Read two long values, print them, then audit the sum: overflow happens when both values are positive and their sum would exceed the maximum long, or when both are negative and their sum would go below the minimum long. Print the safe sum with status OK, or the overflow report.

Input Format:
One line with two long integers separated by a space.

Output Format:
When safe:
Value A: <a>
Value B: <b>
Safe sum: <a + b>
Status: OK
When overflowing:
Value A: <a>
Value B: <b>
Safe sum: overflow
Status: OVERFLOW
Max long: 9223372036854775807

Constraints:
a and b are any two 64 bit long values
questions.sampleoutput2:
Value A: 9000000000000000000
Value B: 9000000000000000000
Safe sum: overflow
Status: OVERFLOW
Max long: 9223372036854775807
questions.output1:
Value A: -8000000000000000000
Value B: -8000000000000000000
Safe sum: overflow
Status: OVERFLOW
Max long: 9223372036854775807
questions.output3:
Value A: 9223372036854775807
Value B: 1
Safe sum: overflow
Status: OVERFLOW
Max long: 9223372036854775807
questions.inputconstrains: a and b are any two 64 bit long values

questions.title: Event Pass with Char Cipher
questions.description:
An event manager prints access passes where each pass carries a secret letter derived with char arithmetic. Read the attendee full name on its own line, then one line with age, tier letter and base price. Tier V gives a 20 percent discount, tier G gives 10 percent, tier P gives none; discounts use integer division. The access code letter is the character A shifted forward by (final price % 26), built with a char cast.

Input Format:
Line 1: full name (may contain spaces)
Line 2: age (an integer), tier (V, G or P), base price (an integer), separated by spaces

Output Format:
Attendee: <name>
Age: <age>
Tier: <tier>
Discount: <base * pct / 100>
Final price: <base - discount>
Access code: <(char) (A + finalPrice % 26)>

Constraints:
1 <= age <= 120, tier is V, G or P, 1 <= price <= 100000
